title: UART Receiver
constraints: 8N1 frames, 8 clock cycles per bit. Call the rising edge that first samples `rx = 0` while idle edge E₀.
At E₀ + 4 (middle of the start bit): if `rx = 1`, it was a glitch, so return to idle.
Data bit i (LSB first) is sampled at E₀ + 12 + 8·i, for i = 0 … 7. The stop bit is sampled at E₀ + 76.
At the stop sample: if `rx = 1`, update `data` and pulse `valid` for one cycle. Otherwise pulse `frame_err` for one cycle and leave `data` unchanged. Return to idle at that same edge.
Synchronous reset: idle, `data = 0`, no pulses. Must be synthesizable.
hints: States: IDLE, then one counter `k` counting edges since E₀. Everything happens at specific values of `k`.
Sampling in the middle of each bit (4 cycles after its start) gives the most noise margin, which is why the start bit is checked at +4.
Shift received bits in from the top (`sh <= {rx, sh[7:1]}`) so that after 8 samples bit 0 sits at `sh[0]`.

examples.title: one byte
examples.input: idle 1s, start bit (8×0), bits of 0xA5 LSB first (8 cycles each), stop bit (8×1)
examples.expected: valid = 1 for one cycle with data = 0xA5, 77 cycles after the start bit began

examples.title: bad stop bit
examples.input: a frame whose stop bit is 0
examples.expected: frame_err = 1 for one cycle, data unchanged
